title: Localization family of a smooth fraction-field subalgebra

source.place: Tag 07BV (lemma-colimit-syntomic), separable-case proof, using Tag 037X (lemma-localization-smooth-separable) and Tag 00T3 (lemma-localize-smooth)

lean.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_fg_localization_family
    {K : Type u} {L : Type v} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    (B : Subalgebra K L) (hBsm : Algebra.Smooth K B)
    (hfrac : IsFractionRing B L) :
    ∃ (ι : Type v) (A : ι → Subalgebra K L),
      Nonempty ι ∧
        (∀ i, Algebra.Smooth K (A i)) ∧
        (∀ i, (A i).FG) ∧
        Directed (· ≤ ·) A ∧
        ∀ x : L, ∃ i, x ∈ A i

statement: Let K and L be fields with an algebra structure K → L, and let B be a smooth K-subalgebra of L such that L is its fraction field. There is a nonempty Type v-indexed family A of smooth finitely generated K-subalgebras of L, directed by inclusion, and every element of L belongs to some A i. Here L : Type v.

proof.text: Index by the nonzero elements f of B. The inclusion B → L extends to φ_f : B[1/f] → L. It is injective because B is a subalgebra of the field L and f is nonzero. Define A_f as its image and identify B[1/f] with A_f by the induced algebra equivalence.

Principal localization is smooth over B; composition with the given smooth K-algebra structure makes it smooth over K. Transport along the algebra equivalence. Smooth algebras have finite presentation and hence finite type, so each A_f is finitely generated.

An element z lies in A_f precisely when z f^n = a for some n ≥ 0 and a ∈ B: use the localization denominator representation in one direction, and the image of a times the nth power of the inverse of f in the other. The index f=1 gives nonemptiness. For f,g ≠ 0, the index fg is nonzero; z f^n=a implies z(fg)^n=ag^n, and z g^n=a implies z(fg)^n=af^n. Thus A_f and A_g are contained in A_fg. Finally write z=a/b with a,b∈B and b≠0 using the fraction-field property. Then zb=a and z∈A_b, giving coverage.
